observation.visible_scene: On a wooden tabletop sits a yellow plastic multi‑blade fish slicer (two facing rows of parallel fins/blades) with a silvery, scaled fish fillet laid across the slots. In the background a wooden cutting board holds two more fish pieces, and a dark knife blade enters from the left edge. Two hands grip the left and right ends of the slicer.
visible_changes: The hands' thumbs and fingers shift their grip, pressing inward and downward on the two blade frames of the slicer (left thumb moves from the side handle toward the top‑left, right thumb from the side handle toward the top‑right).
The upper and lower rows of blades draw slightly closer together around the fish; the fish strip becomes more clearly divided into segments between the fins.
The right index finger comes to rest along the top‑right edge of the device in the later frames.

The combined hands‑and‑slicer assembly tilts and translates a few pixels within the frame, while the cutting board, the two background fish pieces and the knife stay in essentially the same positions, indicating the motion is produced by the hands, not by the camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the fish fillet was originally positioned in the slicer before this excerpt.
Whether the blades fully sever the fish and what happens to the cut pieces afterward.
Whether the device is a hinged clamp or a press‑together tool.
uncertain_details: The exact degree of blade closure / whether cutting is completed within the segment.
Whether the small overall shift of the device is purely hand motion or includes slight camera drift.
The precise material/identity of the fish and of the yellow tool beyond visual appearance.
